stories.title: NASA’s HASP Scientific Balloon Launches from Fort Sumner
stories.summary: The HASP mission was launched on a scientific balloon from NASA’s launch facility in Fort Sumner, New Mexico, at 8:05 a.m. MDT (10:05 a.m. EDT). The balloon and payload reached a float altitude of around 122,000 feet and flew for a total of 6 hours, 45 minutes. This year’s campaign marks the 20th flight for the High-Altitude Student Platform carrying payloads developed by student teams. stories.title: NASA Rocket Takes First Multi-Point Look Inside Radio-Disrupting Clouds
stories.summary: High above Earth, thin veils of metallic haze drift through the edge of space. Known as sporadic E layers, these high-altitude “clouds” form from the vaporized dust of burnt-up meteors, earning their name from the unpredictable way they emerge and then dissipate.
